scenes.title: Domain Model: User
scenes.narration: To keep state predictable and prevent loose dictionaries from circulating across modules, the application defines the User data model. Notice on screen how it establishes a strongly-typed in-memory contract: downstream functions can confidently rely on its attributes without writing defensive runtime assertions everywhere. Whenever you extend this model, maintain this structure so dependent services remain intact.
scenes.takeaway: The User entity provides a typed structure for user attributes (name).
scenes.counterfactual: [HYPOTHETICAL] If a field in User were renamed or made mandatory without default values, all instantiation sites across callers would fail at runtime with a TypeError.

scenes.title: Service Delegation: load_user
scenes.narration: Next, load_user coordinates domain processing by orchestrating calls to sym_e59d8678a1341cfa2534. Rather than performing raw data manipulation itself, it acts as an intermediate business coordinator, delegating specific retrieval tasks while guaranteeing that downstream components receive verified arguments.
scenes.takeaway: load_user cleanly separates entity construction from API transport protocols.
scenes.counterfactual: [HYPOTHETICAL] If load_user returned None instead of a valid entity instance, upstream callers accessing entity attributes would encounter an AttributeError.

scenes.title: API Interface: user_route
scenes.narration: Let's examine how user_route functions as the external gateway for this workflow. Rather than coupling network transport with internal database operations, its primary job is to accept name, validate the incoming payload, and immediately hand off control to domain services. By keeping this gateway lean, changes to HTTP endpoints or web protocols won't destabilize your core business logic.
scenes.takeaway: user_route acts as the boundary between client requests and internal services.
scenes.counterfactual: [HYPOTHETICAL] Modifying the return contract of user_route would require updating all dependent functions that consume its output.

scenes.title: Complete Execution Flow
scenes.narration: Now, let's trace the complete lifecycle of a request as it travels through the application. Execution begins at user_route. Notice how data transitions across each architectural boundary: then request reaches user_route in api.py with name: str., then user_route invokes get_user in app.py., then get_user invokes load_user in app.py., then load_user instantiates class user.. Finally, the terminal result—dict[str, str]—is returned safely to the caller, ensuring a predictable execution lifecycle.

scenes.title: Verified Architecture & Limitations
scenes.narration: In summary, verified static relationships establish the call sequence and data transformations. Runtime database connectivity and network latency remain unverified without live telemetry.
invariants: Typed entity models enforce strict parameter contracts
Gateway routes isolate HTTP interfaces from underlying business domain logic
limitations: Asynchronous external HTTP delays and exceptions are unmodeled
Database connection pools are not statically observable
